Added `Encode(io.Writer) error` and `Decode(io.Reader) error` methods to [`ShapeIndex`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/shapeindex.go#L1562-L1752) and all built-in `Shape` types.

### Summary of Changes

1. **`ShapeIndex` Serialization ([`s2/shapeindex.go`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/shapeindex.go#L1562-L1752))**:
   - Implemented [`Encode(io.Writer) error`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/shapeindex.go#L1562) to serialize `maxEdgesPerCell`, shape slots by shape ID (`nextID`), and full spatial cell structure (`cells` and `cellMap`). Automatically builds unbuilt updates prior to encoding via `maybeApplyUpdates()`.
   - Implemented [`Decode(io.Reader) error`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/shapeindex.go#L1620) to reconstruct index state, shape ID mappings (preserving sparse IDs), spatial cells, and set status to `fresh` so queries/iteration work immediately without needing `Build()`.
   - Added validation against malformed or corrupted inputs, including invalid versions, unknown shape tags, truncated data streams, and bounds on allocation sizes to guard against OOM on malicious or oversized requests.

2. **Built-in `Shape` Type Support**:
   - Added `Encode` and `Decode` methods to [`PointVector`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/point_vector.go#L43-L91), [`LaxPolyline`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/lax_polyline.go#L55-L102), [`LaxPolygon`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/lax_polygon.go#L222-L334), and [`LaxLoop`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/lax_loop.go#L86-L134).
   - Configured non-zero [`typeTag`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/shape.go#L144-L155) values for [`Loop`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/loop.go#L521) (`typeTagLoop`) and [`LaxLoop`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/lax_loop.go#L83) (`typeTagLaxLoop`).
   - Ensured zero-edge shapes and multi-chain shapes round-trip accurately.

3. **Tests ([`s2/shapeindex_test.go`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-msmz_i3o/s2/shapeindex_test.go#L552-L804))**:
   - Added test cases covering empty index encoding, round-tripping of all built-in shape types, shape ID preservation across shape removals, encoding without explicit `Build()`, and decoding malformed or truncated inputs.
